scenario: An Arctic expedition programme shortlists medical officers who possess specialised cold-injury clinical expertise OR logistical-planning proficiency. The two competencies are independent in the candidate pool; OR-gate shortlisting generates a negative within-shortlist correlation.

data.description: Population base rates and OR-gate selection mechanism

values.selection_rule: OR gate: selected if (cold-injury clinical expertise) OR (logistical-planning proficiency)

question: (a) Derive P(selected) from the OR-gate model. (b) Compute P(cold_injury_expertise | ¬logistics_proficiency, selected) and explain why it equals 1. (c) Compute P(cold_injury_expertise | logistics_proficiency, selected) and show it equals P(cold_injury_expertise). (d) Quantify the induced conditional correlation direction and explain why it is a selection artefact rather than a genuine population relationship between cold-injury clinical expertise and logistical-planning proficiency.

ground_truth.explanation: Under OR-gate selection a candidate who lacks logistical-planning proficiency must possess cold-injury clinical expertise to be admitted — hence P(cold_injury_expertise|¬logistics_proficiency,sel)=1.0. A candidate who already has logistical-planning proficiency is admitted regardless of cold-injury clinical expertise, so P(cold_injury_expertise|logistics_proficiency,sel)=P(cold_injury_expertise)=0.44. The gap (1.0 vs 0.44) creates a negative within-selected correlation that is purely a collider-selection artefact.

naive_answer: The negative correlation between cold-injury clinical expertise and logistical-planning proficiency observed among selected candidates reflects a genuine trade-off between these traits in the domain.
naive_trap: The negative correlation is entirely a Berkson collider artefact produced by the OR-gate admission rule; the two traits are independent in the full population.
reasoning_trace: (1) P(sel)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A)P(B)=0.44+0.46-0.44×0.46=0.6976. (2) Among candidates without logistical-planning proficiency: only those with cold-injury clinical expertise are selected → P(cold_injury_expertise|¬logistics_proficiency,sel)=1.0. (3) Among candidates with logistical-planning proficiency: selected regardless of cold-injury clinical expertise → P(cold_injury_expertise|logistics_proficiency,sel)=P(cold_injury_expertise)=0.44. (4) Within-selected: knowing ¬logistics_proficiency raises P(cold_injury_expertise) from 0.44 to 1.0 → negative conditional correlation despite population independence.
python_verification:
pA,pB = 0.44,0.46
pSel = pA+pB-pA*pB
assert abs(pSel-0.6976)<0.005, f'pSel={pSel}'
pA_notB_sel = pA*(1-pB)/(pA*(1-pB))   # =1.0 by definition
assert abs(pA_notB_sel-1.0)<1e-9
pA_B_sel = pA*pB/pB                    # =pA by definition
assert abs(pA_B_sel-0.44)<1e-9
assert pA_notB_sel > pA_B_sel, 'negative collider correlation confirmed'
